description: LLM Model Status SPA foundation - a Svelte 5 SPA served by solar-control at /status, with a read-only aggregation endpoint backed by Redis-cached state (app scaffold, serving modes, build embedding, repo/CI wiring only; page features and data model come later).

userStories.title: Aggregation endpoint GET /api/status in solar-control
userStories.description: As a status page consumer, I need a read-only GET /api/status endpoint that aggregates host/instance/model state from Redis-cached state and DB host rows, so the SPA has a single fast data source without slow live host fan-out.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/status returns JSON aggregating host/instance/model state from Redis-cached state (app/services/host_status.py single-source payload builder) + DB host rows
No live fan-out to hosts (do not call GET /api/models/availability's live per-host fetch path)
Read-only route registered under /api (app/routes/management)
Payload schema defined and recorded when page requirements are specified
solar-control unit tests with mocked Redis stores pass
make lint-solar-control and make test-solar-control pass

userStories.title: Serve built SPA at /status via app.frontend()
userStories.description: As a user, I want solar-control to serve the built SPA at /status when a dist/ build is present, so the production path is same-origin with the control API.
acceptanceCriteria: Register FastAPI app.frontend() via an APIRouter included with prefix /status: router.frontend("/", directory=dist, fallback="auto")
fallback="auto" serves index.html for client-side-routed navigations while missing assets still 404
Regular path operations take precedence: /api and /v1 remain safe
Registered with check_dir=False and a configurable dist path so solar-control starts and tests fine without a build (404 at /status in dev mode)
solar-control unit tests cover serving-with-build and 404-without-build cases

userStories.title: Configurable CORS on solar-control for dev mode
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a configurable CORS policy on solar-control, so the dev SPA can call the control API cross-origin while production stays same-origin and unaffected.
acceptanceCriteria: CORS allow-listed origins via env (CORS_ORIGINS, default empty = CORS disabled)
Same-origin production path unaffected when CORS_ORIGINS is unset
Dev Vite origin can be added locally via env
Unit tests cover enabled and disabled CORS
make lint-solar-control and make test-solar-control pass

userStories.title: Scaffold apps/solar-status (Svelte 5 + Vite + TS)
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a new standalone Svelte 5 + Vite + TypeScript app at apps/solar-status, so the status SPA follows the one-app-one-toolchain convention instead of extending solar-webui (React).
acceptanceCriteria: apps/solar-status scaffolded with Svelte 5 + Vite + TypeScript
apps/solar-status added to pnpm-workspace.yaml members (exact path, like apps/solar-webui)
Conditional Vite base: / for the dev server, /status/ for the production build; verified via import.meta.env.BASE_URL
pnpm install and pnpm --filter solar-status build succeed
No Svelte code added to apps/solar-control (app/ stays purely Python)

userStories.title: Mode-agnostic typed data layer with API base resolution
userStories.description: As the SPA, I need a typed fetch client that resolves the API base URL once at startup, so a single code path works both in dev (absolute VITE_API_BASE) and embedded (relative ../api) modes.
acceptanceCriteria: Typed fetch client; endpoint paths appended to the resolved base (e.g. ${apiBase}/status)
Base resolved once at startup against the mount point: mount = new URL(import.meta.env.BASE_URL, location.origin); apiBase = new URL(import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE ?? "../api", mount)
Resolution independent of the active client-side route; no <base> tag needed
Unit tests cover: absolute base ignores mount anchor; relative base resolves against mount for any route depth
vitest suite passes

userStories.title: Tailwind styling and test tooling in solar-status
userStories.description: As a developer, I want Tailwind and a component test setup in apps/solar-status, so styling stays consistent with solar-webui and UI code is testable.
acceptanceCriteria: Tailwind configured for styling consistency with solar-webui
vitest + @testing-library/svelte configured with at least one smoke test
package.json test/lint scripts work standalone
pnpm --filter solar-status test and lint pass

userStories.title: Dev serving mode: Vite dev server without proxy
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to run the SPA on its own dev server calling solar-control directly, so I can develop the status page without building the SPA or touching the embedded mode.
acceptanceCriteria: Vite dev server on its own port (5174), app served at /, no proxying
.env.development sets VITE_API_BASE=http://localhost:8000
With make dev-control running and the dev origin in CORS_ORIGINS, the page at http://localhost:5174/ loads data from the control API
solar-control runs without any SPA build in this mode

userStories.title: Makefile targets for solar-status
userStories.description: As a developer, I want standard Makefile targets for the new app, so local workflow and CI share the same entry points.
acceptanceCriteria: Makefile targets: dev-status, test-solar-status, lint-solar-status (names match CI matrix app names)
Targets wired into the aggregate test and lint targets
make test and make lint include solar-status
make dev-status starts the Vite dev server per US-007

userStories.title: CI dispatcher and quality gates for solar-status
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want CI isolation for the new app plus explicit coupling to the shared API contract, so Svelte failures don't block solar-control PRs but schema changes still run the SPA's tests.
acceptanceCriteria: ci.yaml dispatcher case for apps/solar-status/* and ALL=1 list entry
solar-control status route/schema paths (app/routes/management status files, app/services/host_status.py) additionally trigger the solar-status gates
quality-gates.yaml: new install branch for solar-status (pnpm + Node 24, mirroring the solar-webui branch)
CI runs green on a sample change in each mapped path

userStories.title: Document apps/solar-status in AGENTS.md
userStories.description: As a contributor, I want the new app documented per repo conventions, so agents and humans know the structure and commands.
acceptanceCriteria: AGENTS.md: apps/solar-status added to the Structure and Commands (Parancsok) sections
User-facing README for the app in Hungarian per conventions
AGENTS.md code/comment language convention respected

userStories.title: Embed SPA build into solar-control Docker image
userStories.description: As an operator, I want the built SPA embedded in the solar-control Docker image, so the production deployment serves /status with no new runtime component.
acceptanceCriteria: solar-control Dockerfile gains a Node build stage that builds the SPA (repo-root build context for lockfile access, like solar-webui) and copies dist/ into the runtime image
.github/release-manifest.json: solar-control context set to "." if required; no new component for the SPA
Image builds successfully; /status serves the SPA in the container
Image size and .dockerignore implications checked
Fixed Docker image names (aiops/*) unchanged

userStories.title: End-to-end verification of both serving modes
userStories.description: As a reviewer, I want both serving modes verified end-to-end, so the foundation is proven before page features are added.
acceptanceCriteria: make lint-solar-status and make test-solar-status pass; full make test lint pass
Mode 1 (dev): make dev-control + make dev-status, page at http://localhost:5174/ renders and calls control on the absolute VITE_API_BASE (CORS allow-list includes dev origin)
Mode 2 (embedded): build the SPA, run make dev-control alone, page at http://localhost:8000/status serves the built assets and works
solar-control unit tests for the new endpoints (mocked Redis stores) pass

userStories.title: Auth gate decision and optional API-key protection
userStories.description: As an operator, I want an optional API-key gate on the status page, so the page does not leak infrastructure details when exposed.
acceptanceCriteria: Decision confirmed: public read-only page vs API-key gate
If gated: optional key via env, mirroring SOLAR_WEBUI_AUTH_KEY behavior
Default configuration unchanged for local/dev use
userStories.notes: Decision to confirm before implementation (see plan's 'Decisions to confirm' section). Feature decisions (payload schema, realtime updates, page contents) are intentionally out of scope for this foundation.
